hints: Start with the word exothermic and remind yourself what it tells you about heat loss and the sign of $\Delta H$.
Remember that breaking bonds takes energy in, while making new bonds releases energy out, and bond energy measures bond strength.
Link the net release of heat to which side must have stronger bonds overall, then match both parts of the statement together.
walkthrough:
**Recall what exothermic means**

Think of exothermic as heat leaving the system to the surroundings. That is why the enthalpy change is always negative.

$$\Delta H \text{ is negative for an exothermic reaction}$$

**Compare breaking and making bonds**

To react, reactant bonds must be broken, which absorbs energy. Then product bonds are formed, which releases energy.

$$\Delta H = \Sigma(\text{bond energies broken}) - \Sigma(\text{bond energies made})$$

**Decide which side has more bond energy**

Since heat is given out overall, more energy must be released on making products than was absorbed on breaking reactants. That can only happen if the products contain stronger bonds in total.

That means total bond energy of products > total bond energy of reactants, with $\Delta H$ negative.

options.A: Half right, half wrong. $\Delta H$ negative is correct for exothermic, but products having less bond energy is backwards. Weaker product bonds would mean less energy released on formation, giving an endothermic result.
options.B: Both parts are wrong for an exothermic reaction. Less product bond energy would mean net energy absorbed, and $\Delta H$ positive describes an endothermic reaction, not an exothermic one.
options.C: Exactly right. Exothermic means net heat released so $\Delta H$ is negative. This happens because stronger bonds are made in the products, so the total bond energy of the products is greater than that of the reactants.
options.D: The bond energy part is correct, products are stronger, but $\Delta H$ positive is wrong. A positive $\Delta H$ means endothermic. An exothermic reaction must have negative $\Delta H$.
